category: Water Ice Deposits and Subsurface Glaciers

catalog.name: Phoenix Arctic Subsurface Ice Table
catalog.discovery_summary: Trenching by robotic scoop exposed pure water ice that sublimated under solar exposure over 4 sols. Covers tens of thousands of square kilometers under a thin desiccated regolith blanket.
catalog.astronaut_in_situ_resource_utilization: Premier source for rocket propellant production (LOX/CH4 via Sabatier) and astronaut life support. Readily excavated with simple mechanical scraping.

catalog.name: Utopia Planitia Subsurface Water Ice Sheet
catalog.discovery_summary: SHARAD radar sounding mapped an enormous underground ice sheet spanning from 39° to 49° N latitude, holding as much fresh water as Lake Superior. Buried beneath 1 to 10 meters of volcanic dust.
catalog.astronaut_in_situ_resource_utilization: Sufficient water reservoir to sustain an permanent human Martian industrial colony for centuries. Lower latitude provides superior solar energy availability compared to polar ice caps.

catalog.name: Korolev Crater Permanent Ice Mound
catalog.mission: Mars Express HRSC & ExoMars TGO CaSSIS
catalog.discovery_summary: An 82-kilometer wide impact crater filled year-round by a dome of pure sparkling water ice nearly 2 kilometers deep. Acts as a cold trap where moving air cools and sinks, forming a perpetual cold protective layer.
catalog.astronaut_in_situ_resource_utilization: Directly accessible surface water ice without drilling through overburden. Visual landmark for northern navigation.

catalog.name: Arcadia Planitia Buried Sheet Ice & Scalloped Depressions
catalog.discovery_summary: Extensive scalloped terrain formed by subsurface permafrost sublimation. Designated by NASA Mars Human Landing Site Study as the #1 candidate landing site due to flat elevation (-3.8 km) and shallow ice table.
catalog.astronaut_in_situ_resource_utilization: Lowest energy expenditure for human crew landing; accessible ice within 1 meter of surface via Rodriguez well melting probes.
